latest_release.name: v2.0.2
latest_release.body:
## Quivr 2.0.2

2.0.2 moves the search database to Weaviate 1.39.14. It changes no API, no configuration and no stored data. Upgrade any 2.0.x installation to it.

### What Weaviate 1.39.14 fixes for Quivr

- **Filtered searches no longer fail at random.** Quivr filters every vector and hybrid search to the scope of the request. Weaviate's default filtering strategy could crash such a search on a node of the vector graph with more links than expected, and the search then returned an error.
- **Security:** CVE-2026-63209, in the compression library.
- **Less memory.**
  - Quivr compresses its vectors. Compressed indexes now drop the uncompressed vector cache they no longer use, which can save gigabytes on a large index.
  - Weaviate also stops keeping memory it never frees when writing to its in-memory tables.
- **Safer restarts.** A crash right after a shutdown could leave a keyword-search file empty, and the database would then not start without a manual repair. Startup and shutdown are also faster.

Results do not change. The hybrid search changes in 1.39.14 only affect `offset` paging and `nearText` queries, and Quivr uses neither.

### Upgrade from 2.0.0 or 2.0.1

1. Back up the search database volume.
2. Deploy the 2.0.2 images and the new Weaviate pin from `deploy/infrastructure.json`, or the 2.0.2 compose bundle attached to this release for a single machine.
3. Keep the same Weaviate volume.

This is a patch upgrade within one Weaviate minor version: no re-indexing and no Quivr migration. The test that upgrades a 1.37.15 volume through 1.38.20 to 1.39.14, then checks lexical, semantic and hybrid search, passes on this release.

The release images are signed and carry SBOMs, as described in [Security of Quivr releases](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/run-quivr/security).

---

# Quivr [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/The-Vibe-Company/quivr) **An open-source engine for content that keeps arriving: store it, search it, and get alerted when something new matches a topic you follow.** You send Quivr documents (news articles, emails, posts, PDFs), or let it collect them from RSS feeds, Microsoft 365 mailboxes and X lists. Quivr keeps every version, makes each document searchable within seconds, and checks it against your saved alerts. Your application talks to Quivr over an HTTP API; Quivr has no user interface of its own. Quivr is developed by [The Vibe Company](https://www.thevibecompany.co), the AI agency created by the Quivr team. > **Status: Quivr 2.** From 2.0.0 on, the HTTP API (`/v0`) stays compatible across > 2.x releases and upgrades keep your data in place; see > [Versions and compatibility](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/reference/compatibility) > and [Known limits](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/reference/known-limits). ## What you can do with it - **Collect content** you send one by one or in batches, or that Quivr pulls from sources on a schedule. Files such as PDFs are read by plugins. - **Search** by keywords, by meaning, or both. Every result points to the exact passage, document and version it comes from, so you can always cite it. - **Follow a topic.** Save an alert such as `"harbour strike" AND (ferry OR port)`, or a plain-language description, and Quivr records every new document that matches, with the reason. Your application reads the matches or receives them as signed webhooks. - **Keep history.** A correction becomes a new version; the old one stays readable. A withdrawn document leaves search at once, and alerts that caught it are told. - **Plug in your own logic.** File formats, sources, embedding models, ranking and alert rules are plugins: small HTTP services you can replace, in any language. - **Let AI agents use it.** `quivr mcp` lets an agent search Quivr and quote what it finds, with the source of every passage. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR sources[Sources and
your application] -->|documents| api[Quivr API] api --> store[(PostgreSQL + object storage
every version, kept safely)] store --> worker[Quivr worker] worker <-->|read, cut, embed,
rank, judge alerts| plugins[Plugins] worker --> index[(Search index)] app[Your application] <-->|search, alerts, changes| api ``` Quivr confirms a document only once it is stored, then processes it in the background: an outage delays processing but never loses what was confirmed. The search index can always be rebuilt from storage. Files such as PDFs are read by plugins. - **Search** by keywords, by meaning, or both. Every result points to the exact passage, document and version it comes from, so you can always cite it. - **Follow a topic.** Save an alert such as `"harbour strike" AND (ferry OR port)`, or a plain-language description, and Quivr records every new document that matches, with the reason. Your application reads the matches or receives them as signed webhooks. - **Keep history.** A correction becomes a new version; the old one stays readable. A withdrawn document leaves search at once, and alerts that caught it are told. - **Plug in your own logic.** File formats, sources, embedding models, ranking and alert rules are plugins: small HTTP services you can replace, in any language. - **Let AI agents use it.** `quivr mcp` lets an agent search Quivr and quote what it finds, with the source of every passage. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR sources[Sources and
your application] -->|documents| api[Quivr API] api --> store[(PostgreSQL + object storage
every version, kept safely)] store --> worker[Quivr worker] worker <-->|read, cut, embed,
rank, judge alerts| plugins[Plugins] worker --> index[(Search index)] app[Your application] <-->|search, alerts, changes| api ``` Quivr confirms a document only once it is stored, then processes it in the background: an outage delays processing but never loses what was confirmed. The search index can always be rebuilt from storage. [How Quivr works](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/how-quivr-works) explains the parts and the guarantees. ## Try it You need Linux on x86_64 or a Mac with Apple Silicon, Docker with Compose v2, the Go version in [`go.mod`](go.mod), Python 3.12 with `venv`, and `jq`. The first start downloads about 1 GB. ```bash git clone https://github.com/The-Vibe-Company/quivr.git && cd quivr make dev # start Quivr and its dependencies in Docker eval "$(make -s env)" # point this shell at the API, with a local key ``` Then follow the [Quickstart](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/quickstart): create a collection, add an article, find it by keyword and by meaning, and get alerted on a topic, in about fifteen minutes. `make demo` adds a web app on top, at http://127.0.0.1:5183 ([`quivr-search/`](quivr-search/README.md)). To install Quivr on a server from published images, without a checkout, see [Run Quivr on one machine](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/run-quivr/single-machine). ## Documentation Everything is on [docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co): | If you want to… | Start with | | --- | --- | | Understand Quivr | [Introduction](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/), then [Core concepts](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/concepts) | | Build an application on it | [Quickstart](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/quickstart), then the guides under *Use Quivr* | | Install and operate it | [Operate a Quivr deployment](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/run-quivr/overview) | | Write a plugin | [How plugins work](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/plugins/overview), then [Build your first plugin](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/plugins/first-plugin) | | Look up an endpoint, command or setting | [Reference](https://docs.quivr.thevibecompany.co/api-reference/overview) | The site's source is [`docs-site/`](docs-site/). Documentation for people changing this repository is listed on [the contributor start page](docs/start/contributor.md). ## Repository layout ```text cmd/quivr/ the single quivr binary: api, worker, migrate, plugin tools, search, mcp internal/ the engine, one Go package per domain module contracts/ the HTTP API (OpenAPI) and plugin protocol contracts sdks/ Go and Python kits for writing plugins plugins/ first-party plugins: alerts, sources, PDF, ingestion, retrieval… client/ Go client generated from the HTTP contract migrations/ PostgreSQL migrations deploy/ Compose, Railway and image build files quivr-search/ demo web app built on the public API docs-site/ the documentation site docs/ contributor docs, decisions (docs/adr/) and dated records (docs/dated/) scripts/ local stack, checks and measurement tooling ``` ## Contributing Read [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for the rules and [`CONTEXT.md`](CONTEXT.md) for the domain vocabulary, then [the contributor start page](docs/start/contributor.md). Run `make check` (about two minutes, no Docker) before pushing; `make verify` runs the end-to-end journeys on an isolated stack. Pull request titles follow Commitizen, for example `feat(ingestion): accept record versions`. Report security issues privately: see [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md). ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
